page.title: Ironman 2032 Marbella: Post-Race Recovery Yacht Charter Guide

data.meta_description: Recharge after Ironman 2032 Marbella with a luxury yacht charter recovery day. Swim, stretch & feast on board – boats from €749/2h. Book now.
data.summary: A post-race recovery yacht charter in Marbella is the ultimate way to unwind after Ironman 2032. Our guide covers the best boats, recovery-friendly itineraries, and everything included – from cold plunges to gourmet snacks.

faq.q: Where does the charter depart from?
faq.a: All boats depart from Puerto Banús, the same location as the Ironman finish line. You walk straight from the race village to the marina – no taxis needed. The marina is also close to Marbella's Golden Mile hotels.

faq.q: Can I book a charter for a large group of athletes?
faq.a: Yes. The Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) and Maiora 26m (26m, 12 pax) are perfect for team recovery. Both have spacious sundecks and saloons. Pricing is on request via WhatsApp – we'll tailor a package with extra snacks and drinks.

faq.q: Is there a minimum age or fitness requirement?
faq.a: No minimum age – families welcome. The skipper handles all navigation. Life jackets are provided for all sizes. If you have mobility issues after the race, let us know and we'll recommend a boat with easy boarding (e.g., the Lagoon 380 catamaran).

faq.q: What if the weather is bad on race day?
faq.a: Marbella enjoys 320 sunny days a year, but if conditions are unsafe, we'll reschedule or refund. The marina is sheltered, and most boats have a covered flybridge or saloon. Check our cancellation policy when booking.

data.body_html:
You've crossed the finish line of Ironman 2032 Marbella. Your muscles are screaming, your mind is buzzing, and the Mediterranean is calling. A post-race recovery yacht charter in Puerto Banús is the smartest way to transition from race mode to relaxation. Within 15 minutes of finishing, you can be on a boat, floating in calm coves, sipping a cold drink, and letting the sea do the healing. Here's how to plan the perfect recovery day on the water.

Why a yacht charter is the ultimate Ironman recovery tool

After 3.8 km of swimming, 180 km of cycling, and 42.2 km of running, your body needs gentle movement, cold exposure, and complete mental reset. A boat delivers all three. The gentle swell massages tired legs, the sea breeze lowers cortisol, and a dip in 18–22 °C water at Cala del Faro reduces inflammation. No gym, no ice bath prep – just step aboard. Our [boat rental Marbella](/fleet/) fleet departs directly from Puerto Banús, so you're on the water within minutes of the finish line.

Best boats for post-race recovery

Choose based on your group size and budget. For a solo or duo recovery, the Dubhe (8 m, 5 pax) is compact and affordable – pricing on request. For small groups, the Astondoa 40 (12.5 m, 9 pax) at €749/2h includes sun pads and a shaded cockpit. The Azimut 39 (12.5 m, 11 pax) at the same rate offers extra seating. For a luxury splurge, the Mangusta 80 (24 m, 12 pax) from €4,719/4h includes a free jet ski for active recovery. All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and 21% IVA.

Sample 4-hour recovery itinerary

  • 11:00 – Board at Puerto Banús. Welcome drink (cava or water).
  • 11:15 – Cruise east toward Cala del Faro (15 min).
  • 11:30–12:30 – Swim stop at Cala del Faro. Gentle floating, light stretching on deck.
  • 12:30–13:00 – Cruise to Cala Cortés. Snacks and drinks served.
  • 13:00–14:00 – Second swim stop. Nap on sun pads.
  • 14:00–14:30 – Return to Puerto Banús.

This itinerary covers two of Marbella's most sheltered coves, with minimal travel time. For a longer day, upgrade to an 8-hour charter (€2,299 on Tier A boats) and add a stop at Cabopino or Estepona.

What's included – and what to bring

Every charter includes: licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA. You don't need to bring anything except sunscreen, a towel, and your post-race compression gear. If you want a proper meal (e.g., paella, salads), let us know via WhatsApp – we can arrange catering. The Ferretti 94 (29 m, 12 pax) has a full galley for food prep.

Cold water recovery – the science and the spots

Cold water immersion reduces muscle soreness and speeds recovery. The Mediterranean off Marbella in late spring/early summer is 18–22 °C – perfect for a 5–10 minute dip. Our recommended spots: Cala del Faro (rocky cove, shallow entry) and Cala Cortés (sandy beach, calm water). Both are within 20 minutes of Puerto Banús. For a longer cruise, Cabo de la Plata near Estepona offers deeper water. Always swim with a buddy – your skipper will monitor conditions.

Nutrition on board – refuel smart

Post-race, your body needs protein, carbs, and electrolytes. Our standard snack pack includes nuts, crisps, olives, and fruit – a good start. We recommend bringing: protein shakes, bananas, recovery bars, and a hearty sandwich. The boats have cool boxes and ice. If you book the Mangusta 80 (white or grey), the crew can prepare light meals. For a full feast, ask about our catering add-on – paella, grilled fish, or salads.

Booking tips for Ironman athletes

Book early – Ironman week is busy. We recommend a 4-hour charter starting at 11:00 – enough time to recover before lunch, swim, and nap. If you're racing in a group, the Ferretti 94 or Maiora 26m (both 12 pax) are ideal. Pricing on request via WhatsApp. For smaller groups, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6 m, 12 pax) offers a flybridge lounge with panoramic views. All boats depart from Puerto Banús – no transfers needed. Check our [full fleet](/fleet/) for availability.
